description: Minority stress: chronic, socially-based stressors distinct from ordinary life events, operating through vigilance, expectation of rejection, and concealment. It is an established framework, not a metaphor.

Not posting about politics. Not joining the protest. Not saying where you studied. Not correcting the interviewer's pronunciation. Each is small and rational; together they are a person continuously editing themselves in case they are being assessed.
energy_note: Managing an audience that may not be watching, because sometimes it is.

aspect: SCENARIO - the protest he walked past
description: Omid was in Tehran in 2022 and walked past a protest without stopping. In 2026 he still thinks about whether a photograph exists, whether it matters for his file, and whether it counts as evidence for or against him depending who is reading. He has never mentioned it to anyone.
energy_note: A memory that is simultaneously your defence and your risk.

aspect: The cost is invisible and therefore uncompensated
description: None of this appears in any refusal letter or any statistic. It is absorbed privately, which is precisely why it never gets counted as part of the cost of the policy.
'So what brought you to Canada?' Omid has four versions of the answer calibrated to how the room feels. The short one, the technical one, the warm one, and the true one, which he has never used.
energy_note: Four rehearsed autobiographies, and none of them yours.
